chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah, from his father, who said:

I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who forgot the adhan and the iqamah until he had entered into the salat (prayer). He said: “Then let him continue in his salat, for the adhan is only a sunnah (prophetic tradition).”

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, the one being asked for the ruling
key_terms.الْأَذَانَ: the call to prayer made before the salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةَ: the second call announcing the immediate commencement of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: a recommended prophetic practice, not an essential pillar here
key_terms.فَلْيَمْضِ: let him continue and proceed without stopping

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets the adhan and iqamah and has already started the salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning one who forgets the adhan and iqamah until after beginning the salat (prayer). Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام instructs that he should continue his prayer, indicating that the adhan is a sunnah (prophetic tradition) and not something that invalidates the prayer if omitted.
